newsitem.title: UK: WORLD BONDS - Gilts to keep poise after RPI data.
newsitem.headline: WORLD BONDS - Gilts to keep poise after RPI data.

text.p: The gilt market should remain well supported on a spread basis after initial jitters on August inflation data faded on Thursday, analysts said.

The numbers, which showed a small fall in year-on-year inflation but were at the top end of analysts' forecasts, slightened dampened arguments for a British interest rate cut soon. But analysts saw little threat to gilts.
"The data are not going to be enough to push the spread meaningfully in one direction or another," said Kevin Adams, gilts analyst at Barclays de Zoete Wedd in London.
The 10-year gilts spread agasint Bunds widened to 174 basis points from 172 before the data. It then moved back to 172.
British retail prices rose 0.5 percent in August, giving a year-on-year rise of 2.1 percent versus 2.2 percent in July. Forecasts had been for 0.4 percent and 2.1 percent respectively.
The analysts said the breakdown of the figures, showing much of the rise to be attributable to increased petrol prices, made the data less disappointing than at first appeared.
Nigel Richardson, head of bond research at Yamaichi International Europe, said the gilt/Bund spread would stick close to current levels.

The 10-year gilt/Bund spread has averaged 165 basis points since last July . The high was the mid-190s in late March/early April, while the low was the low 140s last September and again last December.
Richardson said the spread should widen to about 200 points shortly before a U.K. election next year due to political uncertainty about a Labour government's policies.
Richardson said the next focus for gilt investors would be on an expected bounce in August retail sales data due out next Wednesday which would confirm anecdotal evidence of strong consumer demand.
The consensus forecast is for a monthly rise of 0.4 percent after a 0.6 percent fall in July, and a 3.4 percent year-on year rise compared with 2.2 percent year-on-year in July.

However, Richardson said the dominating factor on the horizon would be the repercussions of any move by the U.S. Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy at the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on September 24.
"We are looking for gilts to be dragged lower along with other European bonds by a U.S. Fed tightening, but within a context of outperformance versus Treasuries," he said.
Richardson suggested gilt investors should favour the short end of the curve in the next three months because of the unlikelihood of any reduction in U.K. interest rates.
Adams said BZW had upgraded U.K bonds to neutral from underweight before Thursday's data.

He said BZW was less worried than before about the medium-term outlook due to growing optimism that goverenment inflation targets would be met and that fiscal discipline would be maintained after the election.
He said it was possible the gilt/Bund spread could come in to about 125 basis points by late next year.
A broker at a gilt-edged market maker said spreads could edge out to about 180 basis points until debt auctions later this month which could present a buying opportunity.
The broker also said the outcome of the September FOMC meeting would be the biggest factor affecting gilts in the short term.

He said gilts would remain affected by concerns about inflation picking up faster in a pre-election situation than in other European countries. At 1120 GMT, the December gilt future contract on LIFFE was trading at 106-20, 3/32 up on the day.
-- Stephen Nisbet, International Bonds +44 171 6320
